sectors.note:
**TL;DR:** Defensive posture dominates market leadership as Energy, Consumer Defensive, and Healthcare sweep all-green breadth while cyclicals and industrials lose ground.

Leadership remains highly concentrated, with only 3 of 11 sectors holding all-green status across all measured time horizons (week, month, quarter, half, and YTD). Energy continues to set the standard at the top spot with a dominant momentum score of 0.967, backed by consistent strength in Healthcare (momentum 0.783). Rotation favored safety over the last 5 sessions, evidenced by Consumer Defensive surging into the top three ranks.

Meanwhile, cyclical and economically sensitive areas are lagging or actively losing momentum. Industrials saw the sharpest short-term degradation, falling two rank spots to 6th, while Consumer Cyclical sits at the bottom of the board with a momentum score of just 0.233. 

## Strength
- Only 3 of 11 sectors register all-green across weekly, monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, and YTD horizons: Energy (momentum 0.967), Consumer Defensive (0.783), and Healthcare (0.783).
- Energy and Healthcare represent sustained leadership, each maintaining top-3 status across 1-, 3-, and 6-month rank profiles.
- Energy holds the commanding #1 YTD rank, anchoring market strength.

## Movers & Momentum
- Consumer Defensive posted the largest short-term advance, jumping +3 spots over 5 sessions to reach rank 3 with a momentum score of 0.783.
- Industrials suffered the steepest drop, sliding -2 spots over 5 sessions to rank 6 (momentum 0.300).
- Basic Materials also slipped, losing -1 spot over the last 5 sessions to land at rank 4 (momentum 0.450).
- Momentum is heavily bifurcated: Energy leads at 0.967, while Consumer Cyclical (0.233), Utilities (0.267), and Real Estate (0.283) occupy the bottom tier.

## Divergences
- Consumer Cyclical is the deepest laggard at rank 11 with 0.233 momentum, diverging starkly from Consumer Defensive, which surged to rank 3 with 0.783 momentum.
- Technology maintains a high rank of 2 YTD despite a middling momentum score of 0.567, trailing the stronger momentum seen in Consumer Defensive (0.783) and Healthcare (0.783).
- Basic Materials and Industrials show short-term weakness (declining 1 and 2 spots, respectively) despite holding mid-tier YTD ranks of 4 and 6.

rotation_phase.label: Defensive
rotation_phase.reasoning: Consumer Defensive and Healthcare are leading alongside Energy while core cyclical sectors like Financials and Technology lag, matching the defensive rotation profile.

- OUT: Industrials -> IN: Consumer Defensive - cyclical leadership faded with Industrials slipping 2 spots (wk=-2.5%, regime=-0.10) while defensive capital surged with Consumer Defensive gaining 3 spots (wk=+5.4%, regime=+0.37, RS-cross-up).
- OUT: Basic Materials -> IN: Energy - capital rotated within resource-linked sectors as Basic Materials dropped 1 spot (mo=-3.9%, regime=-0.33) in favor of Energy displaying strong momentum (wk=+4.5%, mo=+5.0%, RS-cross-up).
sectors.watchlist:
- Basic Materials - Watch for an RS new high confirmation if relative strength pushes further into fresh 20-session highs vs SPY; invalidated if the breakout reverses and RS retreats back below prior resistance levels.
- Consumer Cyclical - Monitor for an RS cross confirmation as relative strength against SPY flips positive, signaling an early rotation; invalidated if RS drops back into negative territory below the benchmark.
- Consumer Defensive - Watch for an RS cross trigger confirmation as relative performance crosses above zero versus SPY; invalidated if the rotation stalls and the RS line falls back below zero.
- Energy - Track the emerging RS cross trigger to see if positive relative strength versus SPY sustains to confirm new rotation; invalidated if the cross fails and RS dips immediately back into the negative.

risk_radar.relative_strength: Energy and Healthcare are decisively beating the S&P 500, with Energy posting an rs_score and rs_confirmed of 1.00 (beating SPY on 7/7 timeframes) and Healthcare recording an rs_score and rs_confirmed of 0.83 (beating SPY on 6/7 timeframes). Both sectors also achieved 20-session RS new highs and registered positive RS crosses alongside Consumer Defensive and Utilities, with Basic Materials and Real Estate joining the RS new highs list, and Consumer Cyclical also registering an RS cross.
risk_radar.risks:
- Consumer Defensive exhibits weak directional consistency, with its rs_confirmed dropping sharply to 0.22 despite an rs_score of 0.67 and beating SPY on 5/7 timeframes.
- Technology similarly shows fragility and fading consistency, holding an rs_confirmed of just 0.22 against an rs_score of 0.67 while beating SPY on only 4/7 timeframes.

industries.note:
**TL;DR:** Energy dominates sustained leadership alongside defensive staples, while broad cyclical and tech groups suffer sharp five-day rank deteriorations.

Leadership remains tightly concentrated in traditional energy and select healthcare names. Integrated Oil & Gas (0.957 momentum) and Refining & Marketing (0.944 momentum) anchor an all-green complex where only 24 of 144 industry groups maintain positive returns across all timeframes. Rotational flows over the past five sessions favored consumer staples, notably Beverages - Wineries & Distilleries (+23 spots) and Confectioners (+13 spots), as well as Medical Distribution (+17 spots).

Conversely, momentum is rapidly bleeding from growth and industrials. Engineering & Construction dropped 26 spots, Software - Infrastructure fell 24 spots, and Internet Retail shed 23 spots over five sessions. Severe laggards remain deeply impaired, led by Advertising Agencies (rank 144, 0.062 momentum), Gambling (rank 143, 0.055 momentum), and Mortgage Finance (rank 142, 0.033 momentum).

## Strength
- Energy maintains an absolute grip on the top tier: Oil & Gas Integrated (0.957 momentum, YTD rank 4), Refining & Marketing (0.944 momentum, YTD rank 1), and Oil & Gas E&P (0.928 momentum, YTD rank 7) are all-green across week, month, quarter, half, and YTD windows.
- Breadth sits narrow with just 24 of 144 groups holding all-green status, led by Medical Distribution (0.880 momentum) and Insurance - Reinsurance (0.85 momentum).
- Sustained multi-month strength is confirmed across Diagnostics & Research, Department Stores (0.83 momentum), and Beverages - Non-Alcoholic, matching the top 36 rank threshold across 1-, 3-, and 6-month metrics.

## Movers & Momentum
- Beverages - Wineries & Distilleries led short-term relative improvement, jumping +23 spots to rank 58 (0.79 momentum), followed by Insurance Brokers (+19 spots to rank 102) and Shell Companies (+19 spots to rank 31).
- Medical Distribution gained +17 spots to reach rank 41, pairing sharp short-term velocity with top-tier 0.880 momentum.
- Severe weekly declines struck Engineering & Construction (-26 spots to rank 51, 0.30 momentum), Software - Infrastructure (-24 spots to rank 57, 0.60 momentum), and Airlines (-21 spots to rank 117, 0.22 momentum).

## Divergences
- Emerging early movers with low baseline momentum include Telecom Services (+11 spots, 0.35 momentum), Packaged Foods (+7 spots, 0.40 momentum), and Restaurants (+7 spots, 0.40 momentum).
- Short-term fatigue is appearing in high-momentum plays: Health Information Services (0.73 momentum) and Real Estate - Diversified (0.64 momentum) both slipped 4 rank spots over the past 5 sessions.
- Copper (0.69 momentum) and Furnishings, Fixtures & Appliances (0.61 momentum) also flashed fading divergence, dropping 1 and 2 spots respectively.
